_comment: Source de verite des prompts. Direction artistique: Grece antique, rendu 3D stylise. La cohesion de la serie ne repose plus sur le texte seul: sheet_terrains est genere en premier et joint en reference (champ `ref`) a chaque tuile. Le script scripts/generate-assets.mjs compose: subject + style[category] + consigne de reference + negative (surchargeable par asset).

assets.subject: A colour and material reference sheet for a board game terrain series, laid out as a single flat grid of exactly ten square panels, five columns by two rows, separated by thin neutral grey gutters. Each panel shows a different terrain surface seen from directly above in strict orthographic projection, densely modelled in three dimensions and full of small crafted objects. Each panel is given a target brightness on a scale where 100 is white and 0 is black; these targets must be followed exactly and never reordered. Top row, left to right: (1) dry Aegean scrubland strewn with pale rocks, small dry shrubs and tufts of grass casting soft little shadows, warm sand, brightness 76; (2) marble quarry, individual pale cut blocks and fallen column drums on shallow quarry steps, soft shading nestling between the blocks, cool grey stone, clearly darker than panel 1, brightness 70, never white, never cracked plaster; (3) barley field, a thick carpet of golden grain in small plots, individual tufts catching the light, a few olive trees at the margins, warm golden, brightness 64; (4) island pasture, springy green grass with small round shrubs, low dry stone walls and a few grazing sheep as soft white shapes, olive green, brightness 57; (5) shallow water over a pale rippled seabed, schools of small fish and scattered rocks visible through it, teal, brightness 51. Bottom row, left to right: (6) terraced clay hillside, short irregular earth terraces facing different directions, held by low dry stone walls, a few potters kilns and stacked amphorae, warm terracotta, distinctly darker than panel 5, brightness 45, no long continuous line and no concentric arc crossing the panel; (7) opaque fog, dense grey-violet mist with soft irregular drifts, nothing identifiable underneath, much darker than any land terrain, brightness 39; (8) deep calm sea, deep blue water with fine even swell and soft light rippling on it, the quietest panel of all but still a living surface, brightness 32; (9) pine and olive woodland, individual rounded tree canopies packed close with soft shadow between them, a few slim cypresses, deep pine green, brightness 25; (10) gold mine, very dark brown-grey rock cut by shallow galleries, timber props and scattered spoil, thin gold veins and nuggets catching the light, the darkest panel of the sheet, brightness 20. The ten panels form one continuous descending ladder of brightness, each panel clearly darker than the one before it and no two panels sharing the same brightness. All ten share one single level of colour saturation: rich and appetising, the colour of a well-made board game, but the same amount of it everywhere — the sea no more saturated than the stone, so that no panel jumps out of the family. Every panel is a real surface densely populated with modelled volumes and soft contact shadows, generous in detail and lively to look at. Not one panel is a flat field of colour or a smooth gradient

assets.note: Planche de serie. Iteration 3. Iteration 1: echelle donnee en relatif -> marbre et garrigue inverses, argile et brume derivees de +33 et +39; et sur-correction du contraste -> huit panneaux sur dix en aplats (contraste 3 a 15). Iteration 2: echelle en valeurs absolues (brightness 76 -> 20). Iteration 3: la bande de saturation est remontee de 14-46 % a 22-58 % et chaque panneau est peuple d'objets modelises — l'harmonie tient a ce que la bande soit etroite, pas a ce qu'elle soit basse, et la serie iteration 1 etait harmonieuse mais eteinte.

assets.subject: Mediterranean woodland seen from directly above, individual rounded pine and olive canopies packed close with soft shadow nestling between them, a few slim cypresses standing among them. Deep pine green clearly dominant. This is panel 9 of the reference sheet, bottom row fourth from the left: one of the two darkest terrains of the series. Canopies of similar size across the whole surface, ground barely visible between them, shadows soft and never black
assets.note: Echelon 9/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Greek island pasture seen from directly above, springy green grass with small round shrubs, a few grazing sheep as soft white shapes, and low dry stone walls. Olive green clearly dominant. This is panel 4 of the reference sheet, top row fourth from the left: a clear step darker than the barley. The walls are short, broken and differently oriented, never a continuous line crossing the surface, never a closed enclosure in the centre
assets.note: Echelon 4/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Ancient Greek barley field seen from directly above, a thick carpet of golden grain with individual tufts catching the light, a few small olive trees scattered through it. Warm gold clearly dominant. This is panel 3 of the reference sheet, top row centre. Plots small, irregular and differently oriented, their edges barely suggested and never continuous — no rectangular grid, no paving, no stone slabs, no tiled pattern, no bare path crossing the surface
assets.note: Echelon 3/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Terraced Greek hillside of red clay seen from directly above, short irregular earth terraces facing different directions, a few potters kilns and stacked amphorae resting among them. Warm terracotta clearly dominant. This is panel 6 of the reference sheet, bottom row far left: a clear step darker than the shallows. Terraces and retaining walls short and broken, no long continuous line, no concentric arc, no parallel bands running across the surface, no stripes
assets.note: Echelon 6/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Greek marble quarry seen from directly above, individual pale cut stone blocks and fallen column drums resting on shallow quarry steps, soft shading nestling between them. Cool grey marble clearly dominant. This is panel 2 of the reference sheet, top row second from the left: clearly darker than the sand of panel 1, and the coolest surface of the series. Blocks of similar size spread evenly, angular cut geometry against organic ground, no dominant ridge line, no deep shadow pit, never white, never cracked plaster, no snow
assets.note: Echelon 2/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Dry Aegean scrubland seen from directly above, strewn with pale rounded rocks, small dry shrubs and tufts of golden grass, each object modelled in soft volume with a small contact shadow beneath it. Warm sand clearly dominant. This is panel 1 of the reference sheet, top row far left: the lightest terrain of the whole series. Objects scattered evenly across the whole surface, none larger than the others, almost flat ground beneath them
assets.note: Echelon 1/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Calm deep Aegean sea seen from directly above, deep blue water with a fine even swell and soft light rippling across it, the surface alive with small highlights everywhere. Deep blue clearly dominant. This is panel 8 of the reference sheet, bottom row centre: the least eye-catching surface of the whole series, but never an empty one — the ripples must be visible everywhere rather than leaving a flat field of colour. No swirls, no large wave pattern, no foam, no coastline, no land, no reflection of anything
assets.note: Echelon 8/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Ancient Greek gold mine seen from directly above, very dark brown-grey rock cut by shallow galleries, timber props and scattered spoil heaps, thin gold veins and small nuggets catching the light. This is panel 10 of the reference sheet, bottom row far right: the darkest surface of the whole series. The rock itself stays desaturated and the gold is the only bright accent, thin and evenly scattered — no bright centre, no glow, no large gold mass
assets.note: Echelon 10/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Shallow Aegean water seen from directly above, a pale rippled seabed with schools of small fish and scattered rocks visible through the clear water. Teal clearly dominant. This is panel 5 of the reference sheet, top row far right: clearly darker than the pale stone terrains, and clearly lighter than the open sea. Deep enough that the water carries real colour rather than reading as pale sand, ripples fine and even, no coastline, no foam, no beach
assets.note: Echelon 5/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.

assets.subject: Thick opaque fog seen from directly above, dense grey-violet mist with soft irregular drifts and real depth in it, nothing identifiable underneath. This is panel 7 of the reference sheet, bottom row second from the left: distinctly darker than every land terrain and lighter than the sea, and clearly violet rather than neutral grey. No repeated spiral motif, no curling volutes arranged in a pattern, no flat grey field
assets.note: Echelon 7/10 de l'echelle de valeurs, du plus clair au plus sombre.
